## Maple review 🟡 **Confidence 6/10** · needs attention Three confirmed behavior bugs in new derivation and payload code, none pinned by a test: the slug, the settings dirty comparison and the swallowed monitors read. 3 warnings −3 · 2 notes · tests partial −1 · risk medium Adds the Status pages tab to the alerts page and a full page editor (components, incidents, settings) with its route. The shell holds up, but the slug suggestion and the settings save-dirty tracking are wrong, and two monitor-read failures are swallowed into an all-green view. The ten open `McpQueryError` issues in `page/registry.ts` are untouched: the diff only registers the new page there. - `listPageSummaries` derives each page's worst status and open-incident count for the hub tab - `AlertsStatusPage` route and page keyed by `pageId` open the editor at `/alerts/status-pages/$pageId` - Editor writes supersede their own reads; settings edits live behind a save bar - Break-glass token, publish and delete stay behind `model.isAdmin` ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F1 · slugFromName turns NFKD combining marks into hyphens correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/slug.ts:12-13`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/089c3f95a437ec7ea114542c096771683a66cd8f/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/slug.ts#L12-L13) `.normalize("NFKD")` splits an accented letter into base + combining mark, and `/[^a-z0-9]+/gu` then matches that mark as a separator, so the suggested address for "Crème Brûlée" is `cre-me-bru-le-e` and for "Über" is `u-ber` (run against the head checkout). The user has to retype every suggestion that carries a diacritic. ``` .normalize("NFKD") .replace(/\p{M}+/gu, "") .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gu, "-") ```
🟠 Warning · F2 · isSameSettings compares raw drafts to the normalized page, so a save never settles correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/form.ts:249-257`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/089c3f95a437ec7ea114542c096771683a66cd8f/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/form.ts#L249-L257) `settingsPayload` trims `description`/`websiteUrl`/`logoUrl` (`orNull`, `form.ts:69`) and lower-cases `brand_color` (`form.ts:289`), so after a successful save `savedSettings` compares e.g. `"#AABBCC"` or `"Acme! "` against the server's `"#aabbcc"` / `"Acme!"`, `isCaughtUp` is false and `settingsEdits` is never cleared: the save bar stays up and `isSettingsDirty` (`update-settings.ts:37`) keeps the page dirty however many times the user saves. ``` /** The values the API echoes back: trimmed, and the color lower-cased, as `settingsPayload` sends. */ const normalizedSettings = (form: SettingsForm): SettingsForm => ({ ...form, name: form.name.trim(), description: form.description.trim(), websiteUrl: form.websiteUrl.trim(), logoUrl: form.logoUrl.trim(), brandColor: form.brandColor.trim().toLowerCase(), }) export const isSameSettings = (a: SettingsForm, b: SettingsForm): boolean => { const [left, right] = [normalizedSettings(a), normalizedSettings(b)] return ( left.name === right.name && left.slug === right.slug && left.description === right.description && left.websiteUrl === right.websiteUrl && left.logoUrl === right.logoUrl && left.brandColor === right.brandColor && left.showPoweredBy === right.showPoweredBy && left.autoIncidents === right.autoIncidents ) } ```
🟠 Warning · F3 · orElseSucceed(() => []) on the monitors read reports every monitor-backed component Operational correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/shared/status-page-commands.ts:49`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/089c3f95a437ec7ea114542c096771683a66cd8f/apps/web/src/page/alerts/shared/status-page-commands.ts#L49) When `uptimeMonitors.list` fails, `monitors` becomes `[]`, so `componentStatus` (`status-page-derive.ts:86`) finds no monitor for a monitor-backed component and `deriveComponentStatus` returns `operational`: the Status pages tab renders an all-green page with zero open incidents while the monitor data is unavailable, and nothing on the tab says the read failed. Carry the failure into the same `toLoadFailure` as the page and incident reads. ``` listMonitors, ```
🔵 Note · F4 · ClickedRetry never re-reads monitors correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update.ts:148-154`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/089c3f95a437ec7ea114542c096771683a66cd8f/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update.ts#L148-L154) The editor reads monitors in `init` (`update.ts:111`) but the retry available from every error state only supersedes page, components and incidents, so a failed monitors read is never retried: `monitorsOf(model)` stays `[]` for the life of the mount and the component dialog's monitor select (`view-components.ts`) offers only "None", with no other way to recover short of a reload. ``` ClickedRetry: () => chain( model, readPage(context, "Supersede"), readComponents(context, "Supersede"), readIncidents(context, "Supersede"), readMonitors(context, "Supersede"), ), ```
🔵 Note · F5 · Whitespace in Address sets isSlugEdited while storing an empty slug correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/list/update.ts:75`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/089c3f95a437ec7ea114542c096771683a66cd8f/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/list/update.ts#L75) `slug: value.trim().toLowerCase()` with `isSlugEdited: value !== ""` leaves `slug: ""` and the flag set as soon as a space is typed, so `ChangedName` stops deriving the address, `list/view.ts:172` hides the address issue for an empty slug, and Create stays disabled with nothing saying why. ``` model: { ...model, slug: value.trim().toLowerCase(), isSlugEdited: value.trim() !== "" }, ```

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Held at 8 because a warning is open. 1 warning −1 · 2 notes · tests covered · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable Adds the customer status-page tab and editor (components, incidents, settings) to the alerts hub, plus the API/MCP surface behind it. The three earlier web bugs are fixed. One new bug: incident publish is a second write, so a failed publish duplicates the update on retry. The open `McpQueryError` issues from `registry.ts` are untouched by this diff. - `/alerts?tab=status-pages` lists pages with derived worst status and open incidents - Editor tabs for components, incidents and settings; page controls admin-gated only - `slugFromName` strips combining marks and `isSameSettings` compares normalized drafts - `post_status_page_update` publishes a draft after posting the update ### Before merge - [ ] **Infra** · Check every environment has what this config now expects · [`alchemy.run.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/f7a25c01c357d775ea80c217637523be4377229d/alchemy.run.ts) ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F6 · post_status_page_update commits the public update before publishing it correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:492-497`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/f7a25c01c357d775ea80c217637523be4377229d/apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts#L492-L497) `publish: true` on a draft posts the update first and then publishes in a second write; if `updateIncident({ published: true })` fails, the tool returns an error while the customer-readable update is already stored. The model retries, a second identical update is appended, and once a publish succeeds both appear on the public page. Make the update and its publish one service call (a `publish` flag on `StatusPagesService.postUpdate`, or one transaction) so a failure leaves neither. ``` Add a `publish` flag to `StatusPagesService.postUpdate` and set `published` in the same write as the update, then call it once from this handler instead of following up with `updateIncident`. ```
### Still open from earlier reviews - 🔵 **Note** · F4 · `ClickedRetry` never re-reads monitors · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update.ts:148`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/f7a25c01c357d775ea80c217637523be4377229d/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update.ts#L148) - 🔵 **Note** · F5 · Whitespace in Address sets `isSlugEdited` while storing an empty slug · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/list/update.ts:75`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/f7a25c01c357d775ea80c217637523be4377229d/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/list/update.ts#L75) ### Fixed since the last review - ✅ ~~F1 · `slugFromName` turns NFKD combining marks into hyphens~~ - ✅ ~~F2 · `isSameSettings` compares raw drafts to the normalized page, so a save never settles~~ - ✅ ~~F3 · `orElseSucceed(() => [])` on the monitors read reports every monitor-backed component Operational~~ ### Production impact

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge One confirmed defect: the editor folds monitor and incident read failures into empty data and shows the page as healthy. 1 warning −1 · tests partial −1 · risk medium Adds a Status pages tab to the alerts hub and a full editor for components, incidents and settings. Mergeable once the editor stops reporting failed monitor and incident reads as healthy. The McpQueryError issues in the page registry are not touched by this diff. - `listPageSummaries` derives each hub row's worst component status and open incident count - The editor reads page, components, incidents and monitors once and re-reads after every write - Settings edits sit behind a normalized save bar with publish, break-glass token and delete - All write actions are gated on `isAdmin` with the busy flag guarding replay ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F7 · A failed monitors or incidents read reads as every component Operational in the editor correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/reads.ts:98`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/20e9e75a86f6b8c41ec55dce2a46fd16b7d8f39e/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/reads.ts#L98) `monitorsOf` and `incidentsOf` fold a `Failure` into `[]`, and the editor only surfaces failures for `model.components` and `model.incidents` (`editor/view.ts:128-142`), so a failed `uptimeMonitors.list` leaves `monitorStatus` null and `deriveComponentStatus` (`packages/domain/src/status-page.ts:300`) returns `operational`: the header badge and every monitor-backed row read green while monitoring is unavailable. Worse, the component dialog's linked-monitor select then offers only "None" (`view-components.ts:223`), so saving an unrelated edit on a monitored component sends `monitor_id: null` and silently drops the link — the list tab deliberately fails the whole read for exactly this reason (`shared/status-page-commands.ts:49`). ``` Make `readMonitors`' and `readIncidents`' failures reach the editor the way the list tab does: have `tabRead`/the page header check `model.monitors.data` (and `model.incidents.data`) and render `errorState` with `ClickedRetry` instead of folding them to `[]`, and disable the component dialog while monitors are failed/loading. ```
### Fixed since the last review - ✅ ~~F4 · `ClickedRetry` never re-reads monitors~~ - ✅ ~~F5 · Whitespace in Address sets `isSlugEdited` while storing an empty slug~~ - ✅ ~~F6 · `post_status_page_update` commits the public update before publishing it~~ ### Production impact

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Held at 8 because a warning is open. 1 warning −1 · tests covered · risk medium · 2/2 new units observable Adds the Status pages tab to the alerts hub and a per-page editor for components, incidents, settings and publishing. Safe to merge apart from the incidents tab rendering while the components read failed; the MCP `McpQueryError` issues in maple-ai/maple-chat are untouched by this web-only diff. - `/alerts?tab=status-pages` lists pages with worst status, open incidents and publish state - Components tab and status badge now wait on the components, monitors and incidents reads - Component reorder is optimistic and re-reads on failure - Settings save bar, break-glass token and page delete are admin-only, matching the API ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F8 · Incidents tab renders while the components read failed, so the page looks like it has none correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/view.ts:132-136`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/03e61595034e39010660f6b8459ee1091a05bc44/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/view.ts#L132-L136) `tabRead` waits only on `model.incidents.data` for the incidents tab, yet that tab's cards and composer read `componentsOf(model)`. When the components read fails and the incidents read succeeds, the tab renders and the composer says "The page has no components yet." while the incidents cards say "No components named", so a member opens an incident with no affected components and never sees the failure or its retry. ``` Fold the components read into the incidents branch the way the components branch folds monitors and incidents: `failure: AsyncData.getError(model.incidents.data).pipe(Option.orElse(() => AsyncData.getError(model.components.data)))`, `isReady: AsyncData.hasData(model.incidents.data) && AsyncData.hasData(model.components.data)`. ```
### Fixed since the last review - ✅ ~~F7 · A failed monitors or incidents read reads as every component Operational in the editor~~ ### Production impact

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 10/10** · safe to merge A well-tested Foldkit UI change; the only open defect is the tab-based error title at `view.ts:161`, which the new scene test now pins. 3 notes · tests covered · risk medium Adds the Status pages tab to the alerts hub and a components/incidents/settings editor for one page. Contained web UI with scene coverage; the open `McpQueryError` issues in `registry.ts` are not addressed by the two route lines this PR adds there. - `pageCount` and the tab bar add a Status pages tab wired through `StatusPages.request` - The editor waits on every read a tab consumes and shows `errorState` with Retry - `moveComponent` writes the new order optimistically, then re-reads components and page ### Findings
🔵 Note · F10 · The reorder test never renders the optimistic order its title claims tests · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/editor.scene.test.ts:144`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/c7c746f89fb1d94be3cec984c73b8d13c1611a37/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/editor.scene.test.ts#L144) The test is titled "…and shows it at once", but it only inspects `moving.commands`; the command's `componentIds` come from the local `next` list, not from the `AsyncData.map` write to `model.components` (`update-components.ts:122`). > [!WARNING]
> **`slugFromName` turns NFKD combining marks into hyphens**
>
> <sub>F1 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`.normalize("NFKD")` splits an accented letter into base + combining mark, and `/[^a-z0-9]+/gu` then matches that mark as a separator, so the suggested address for "Crème Brûlée" is `cre-me-bru-le-e` and for "Über" is `u-ber` (run against the head checkout). The user has to retype every suggestion that carries a diacritic.

```
Strip the combining marks NFKD produces before turning separators into hyphens.
```

```suggestion
		.normalize("NFKD")
		.replace(/\p{M}+/gu, "")
		.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gu, "-")
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`isSameSettings` compares raw drafts to the normalized page, so a save never settles**
>
> <sub>F2 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`settingsPayload` trims `description`/`websiteUrl`/`logoUrl` (`orNull`, `form.ts:69`) and lower-cases `brand_color` (`form.ts:289`), so after a successful save `savedSettings` compares e.g. `"#AABBCC"` or `"Acme! "` against the server's `"#aabbcc"` / `"Acme!"`, `isCaughtUp` is false and `settingsEdits` is never cleared: the save bar stays up and `isSettingsDirty` (`update-settings.ts:37`) keeps the page dirty however many times the user saves.

```
Compare the normalized values both sides, not the raw drafts against the saved page.
```

```suggestion
/** The values the API echoes back: trimmed, and the color lower-cased, as `settingsPayload` sends. */
const normalizedSettings = (form: SettingsForm): SettingsForm => ({
	...form,
	name: form.name.trim(),
	description: form.description.trim(),
	websiteUrl: form.websiteUrl.trim(),
	logoUrl: form.logoUrl.trim(),
	brandColor: form.brandColor.trim().toLowerCase(),
})

export const isSameSettings = (a: SettingsForm, b: SettingsForm): boolean => {
	const [left, right] = [normalizedSettings(a), normalizedSettings(b)]
	return (
		left.name === right.name &&
		left.slug === right.slug &&
		left.description === right.description &&
		left.websiteUrl === right.websiteUrl &&
		left.logoUrl === right.logoUrl &&
		left.brandColor === right.brandColor &&
		left.showPoweredBy === right.showPoweredBy &&
		left.autoIncidents === right.autoIncidents
	)
}
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`post_status_page_update` commits the public update before publishing it**
>
> <sub>F6 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`publish: true` on a draft posts the update first and then publishes in a second write; if `updateIncident({ published: true })` fails, the tool returns an error while the customer-readable update is already stored. The model retries, a second identical update is appended, and once a publish succeeds both appear on the public page. Make the update and its publish one service call (a `publish` flag on `StatusPagesService.postUpdate`, or one transaction) so a failure leaves neither.

```
Add a `publish` flag to `StatusPagesService.postUpdate` and set `published` in the same write as the update, then call it once from this handler instead of following up with `updateIncident`.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **A failed monitors or incidents read reads as every component Operational in the editor**
>
> <sub>F7 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`monitorsOf` and `incidentsOf` fold a `Failure` into `[]`, and the editor only surfaces failures for `model.components` and `model.incidents` (`editor/view.ts:128-142`), so a failed `uptimeMonitors.list` leaves `monitorStatus` null and `deriveComponentStatus` (`packages/domain/src/status-page.ts:300`) returns `operational`: the header badge and every monitor-backed row read green while monitoring is unavailable. Worse, the component dialog's linked-monitor select then offers only "None" (`view-components.ts:223`), so saving an unrelated edit on a monitored component sends `monitor_id: null` and silently drops the link — the list tab deliberately fails the whole read for exactly this reason (`shared/status-page-commands.ts:49`).

```
Make `readMonitors`' and `readIncidents`' failures reach the editor the way the list tab does: have `tabRead`/the page header check `model.monitors.data` (and `model.incidents.data`) and render `errorState` with `ClickedRetry` instead of folding them to `[]`, and disable the component dialog while monitors are failed/loading.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Incidents tab renders while the components read failed, so the page looks like it has none**
>
> <sub>F8 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`tabRead` waits only on `model.incidents.data` for the incidents tab, yet that tab's cards and composer read `componentsOf(model)`. When the components read fails and the incidents read succeeds, the tab renders and the composer says "The page has no components yet." while the incidents cards say "No components named", so a member opens an incident with no affected components and never sees the failure or its retry.

```
Fold the components read into the incidents branch the way the components branch folds monitors and incidents: `failure: AsyncData.getError(model.incidents.data).pipe(Option.orElse(() => AsyncData.getError(model.components.data)))`, `isReady: AsyncData.hasData(model.incidents.data) && AsyncData.hasData(model.components.data)`.
```
